list: The official 55 trophies, with a guide to each in the Atlas's own words

sources.official: Official trophy descriptions — PlayStation, as listed by Exophase and PSNProfiles (the two agree on every name, description and grade)
sources.psnprofiles: PSNProfiles — the progress target (count) PlayStation tracks for this trophy
sources.own: Vice Trophy Atlas — the Atlas's own advice

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum lands the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, so there is nothing to do for this one directly — it is the finish line, not a task. Plan around it instead: the roadmap's five stages are ordered so the missable trophies come first and the long grinds come last, and the final stage is the cleanup that leaves this trophy as the last pop. If the counter still shows 54 of 55, the checklist's missing filter shows exactly which trophy is left.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: This is the opening mission, Gone Fishing, and it unlocks through normal story play — no detour and no preparation needed. Play the first mission to its end and the trophy pops with the mission-complete screen. It is the natural first bronze of the set, so if it has not popped, simply keep playing the story.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 1 and the trophy pops when the chapter closes. Chapters are linear, so the only way to miss it is to stop playing — there is no side requirement. Use the chapter to learn the map and the driving, because the later chapters assume both.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 2 and the trophy pops at the chapter's end. While the chapter runs, keep an eye out for the partner trophies that share its missions — Hot Together and Retail Therapy both need your partner beside you, and the chapter is the easiest place to set them up. Missable trophies are flagged in the Missables tab; check it before the chapter closes.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 3 and the trophy pops when the chapter closes. By this point the map is open enough to start the exploration trophies in parallel — discovering vehicles and areas counts whenever you drive, so let the travel between missions do double duty. The checklist's stage filter shows which stage-3 trophies are already progressing.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.guide: Finish every mission in Chapter 4 and the trophy pops at the chapter's end. This is the last full chapter before the finale, so before starting its final mission, sweep the missables list one more time — several one-shot trophies (Cal's fishing challenge, Bret's hunt, the partner moments) only happen while the story still offers them. Anything flagged missable and still unearned deserves a manual save first.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.guide: Finish the final mission and this gold pops with the credits. It is unmissable as long as the story is finished, but do not rush into it: once the finale is done, several story-locked moments close for good. Clear every missable trophy first, then walk into the finale knowing the cleanup stages are all that remain.

trophies.name: Trust
trophies.guide: Complete the mission Breakfast Run when the story offers it. Named-mission trophies like this one pop at the mission-complete screen with no extra condition, so just play the mission through. If the mission is not in your mission list yet, keep playing the story — it appears in sequence.

trophies.name: Break the Bank
trophies.guide: Complete the mission The Cartel Heist when the story offers it. Heist missions tend to be longer and to gate later story beats, so finish it before chasing side content that needs the later map. The trophy pops at the mission-complete screen.

trophies.name: Family Matters
trophies.guide: Complete the mission Child's Play when the story offers it. Like the other named-mission trophies, it needs nothing beyond finishing the mission itself — no rating, no optional objective. Play it through and the trophy follows.

trophies.name: DWNFALL
trophies.guide: Complete the mission Headliners when the story offers it. Named missions appear in story order, so if Headliners is not available yet, the earlier missions are the blocker. Finish the mission and the trophy pops at the complete screen.

trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
trophies.guide: Complete the mission VCIA Takedown when the story offers it. The airport area matters for more than this mission — the one-shot departure trophy, Catch Me If You Can, also happens at VCIA, so learn the airport's layout while you are here. The trophy itself pops at the mission-complete screen.

trophies.name: Snow Storm
trophies.guide: Complete the mission Operation Savage Glory when the story offers it. Operations are usually the bigger set pieces of a chapter, so stock up on armour and ammo before starting rather than mid-mission. Finish it and the trophy pops at the complete screen.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion, which the game tracks across story missions, stranger strands, collectibles, activities and the exploration totals — it is the sum of almost everything else on this list, so it falls last or second-to-last. The practical way to chase it is the checklist itself: filter by missing, work stage by stage, and let the completion percentage in the game's own stats screen confirm what is left. Do not expect it before the story is done and the collectibles are finished.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts — jumps, near misses, drifts and airtime all count toward the running total, and PlayStation tracks the count for you. The fastest honest way is to fold stunting into everything else: take jumps on the way to missions, drift through corners, and use ramps whenever one is in front of you. It is a grind best done passively across the whole playthrough rather than in one sitting; if it is the last silver standing, pick a fast car and a stretch of open road and chain jumps. Flagged as a stage-2 activity: start it early, finish it late.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try each of the 9 activity types once — one go at each is enough, no win or score required. The activities are the ones this list tracks elsewhere: stunts, the shooting range, drone races, races, fishing, the arcade, bowling, meditation and the stranger-style side content. The practical route is a sampler tour: visit each activity once during stage 2 and tick it off as you go, so the trophy pops the moment the ninth type is tried.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in all 42 Shooting Range challenges — every challenge, not just most of them, so a single silver medal blocks the trophy. Treat it as a skill grind: learn one weapon class at a time, replay the challenges you miss until they turn gold, and use the range's own scoring feedback to see which shots cost you. It pairs well with the combat trophies, since the same aim practice feeds Combat Focus kills.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations — each location needs its own win, so one fast course is not enough. Learn the drone's handling on the easiest location first, then work through the list location by location; the races are short, so a loss costs minutes, not hours. Check the map for unvisited race spots when the count stalls.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different courses count, repeats of the same course do not, so variety is the requirement. Run the race types you are best at first (street, off-road, whatever suits your driving), and keep a mental list of which courses are already won. The drone races do not count here; these are the driving races.

trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge — a one-shot story moment, so it is flagged missable: it happens when Cal offers the challenge during the story, and there is no second invitation once that moment passes. Save before taking the challenge, learn the fishing timing on the first cast, and beat his catch. If the challenge is already behind you and the trophy has not popped, the moment is gone for this playthrough.

trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
trophies.guide: Complete one arcade game — finish a full game at any arcade cabinet, any title, any score. It is the easiest activity trophy on the list: walk into an arcade, pick the shortest game, and play it to the end. Do it during the stage-2 activity sweep, when the other one-shot activities are already on your route.

trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Andy's strand. Character strands unlock as the story progresses and end with a final mission of their own — play Andy's missions in order until the strand closes and the trophy pops. If Andy's missions are not showing, advance the main story until they appear.

trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Kenton's strand. Like the other character strands, Kenton's missions appear in story order and close with a final mission — play them through in sequence and the trophy pops at the strand's end.

trophies.name: The Lone Rider
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Billy's strand. Billy's missions arrive in story order; play each one as it appears and the strand closes with its final mission and this trophy. Strands are easy to leave half-finished while chasing the main story, so check the mission list before moving to the next chapter.

trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks
trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete 8 stranger mission strands across Leonida — eight full strands, not eight missions. Strangers appear as map icons around the state; each strand is a short chain that ends with its own closing mission. The practical route is to take every stranger icon you pass while exploring, since the strands are scattered and the count only moves when a whole strand finishes. Andy's, Kenton's, Billy's, Randy's and Tyrone's strands all count toward the eight.

trophies.name: Supply & Demand
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Randy's strand. Randy's missions unlock in story order like the other character strands; play them in sequence until the strand closes. It counts toward Strangers & Freaks, so finishing Randy's strand moves two trophies at once.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Complete the final mission in Tyrone's strand. Tyrone's missions arrive in story order; play them through until the strand's final mission and the trophy pops. With Randy's, Billy's, Kenton's and Andy's strands, Tyrone's is one of the five named strands that feed the eight-strand silver.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 spots across Leonida — every spot, so one missed location blocks the trophy. Meditation spots are quiet scenic points scattered around the state; the count is tracked, so check it after each session to confirm the spot registered. The efficient route is a dedicated sweep: work region by region with the map open, ticking spots off as you go, rather than hoping to stumble on all eighteen.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret — a one-shot story moment, so it is flagged missable: Bret's hunt comes up once during the story, and the unique animal will not wait for a later chapter. Save before the hunt, follow Bret's lead to the animal, and take the shot cleanly. Missing the moment means missing the trophy for this playthrough.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.guide: Complete 3 collectible card sets — three full sets, so scattered single cards do not count. Cards are tucked around Leonida in shops, hideouts and mission areas; the set structure means you need every card of a set, not just most of them. The practical approach is to finish one set at a time: pick the set with the fewest cards missing, hunt those down, and let the silver pop when the third set completes.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.guide: Use WAiNK It at 100 locations — one hundred distinct spots, so repetition does not help. WAiNK It is the in-world photo-sharing habit: open it at landmarks, viewpoints and street corners as you travel, and the count climbs with your exploration. Fold it into the stage-3 map sweep: every area you visit for the 52-area trophy is a chance to WAiNK It, so the two trophies progress together.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.guide: Complete 50 challenges — the game's running list of small feats, from driving and combat to exploration and activities. The count is cumulative across everything you do, so it grows fastest when you play widely rather than grinding one thing: mix missions, activities and free roam and the challenges tick over on their own. If it stalls near the end, open the challenges list in-game and pick off the cheapest ones left.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star wanted level with your partner beside you and escape the heat — flagged missable because it needs your partner present, and partner missions thin out as the story ends. Set it up deliberately: start from a partner mission, build the wanted level to four stars, then break line of sight and stay hidden until it clears. Do it while the story still pairs you up; after the finale there may be no partner to lose the heat with.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your wanted level — flagged missable because it needs your partner beside you, and the window for partner play closes as the story ends. Pick three shops close together, plan the route before the first robbery, keep it quick and keep your partner in the car between stops. If the wanted level drops between shops, the chain breaks and you start over. Do it during the story, not after.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.guide: Discover 100 vehicles — drive or sit in one hundred different vehicles and the count moves. Variety is the whole requirement: the same model twice does not count twice. The count grows naturally if you steal whatever is parked nearby instead of always taking your favourite car, and it pairs with the exploration sweep — new areas hold new vehicles. If it stalls late, cruise car parks, dealerships and highway traffic for models you have not driven.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus — five kills inside one activation, so it is about the setup, not the shooting. Wait for a fight with a crowd: a gang shootout, a police response, or a mission with grouped enemies. Trigger Combat Focus only when five targets are in front of you, and keep firing until the focus ends. Practise the timing at the shooting range first, since the same aim work feeds The Shootist.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA, the airport — flagged missable because it is a single improvised moment, not a repeatable activity: grab a plane at the airport and take off without a flight plan. The clean way is to drive onto the airfield, take any plane, and get airborne before security closes in. Save before trying it, since a failed attempt can end with a wanted level and a wrecked plane.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Deal with the Rhinos — the tanks — in whatever way the moment demands. The description is deliberately vague, which is the hint: this is a one-off encounter with military hardware, flagged missable because the Rhinos show up in a specific situation rather than on demand. When a wanted level or a mission brings armour onto the streets, deal with it then — steal one, destroy one, or survive one, as the moment allows. Keep a save from before any military response so a failed try costs nothing.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected — no alarms, no witnesses raising the alarm, in and out clean. Scout the store first: learn the guard patrols and the camera angles, go in quiet, take the goods and leave before anyone notices. If the alarm trips, the attempt is spent — leave, lose the heat, and try again with a better plan. A silenced approach and a fast car outside make the difference.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.guide: Rob 5 bank vaults and escape — five separate vault jobs, each ending with a clean getaway. Bank vaults are the biggest heists on the list, so plan each one: the approach, the vault itself, and above all the escape route, since the trophy only counts when you get away. Spread them across the crime stage rather than back-to-back, and restock armour and ammo between jobs.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape — stop one, crack it open, take the cash and get away clean. Armored trucks run set routes around the city, so watch for one, block it, deal with the guards fast, and have your getaway car pointed at open road before you start. The trophy pops when the escape is complete, not when the truck opens.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.guide: Explore all 52 areas of Leonida — every named area on the map, from Vice City's districts to the swamps and the Keys. The count is tracked, so the map itself tells you what is left: open it, look for the areas you have never entered, and drive through them. The efficient route is a full-map sweep in stage 3, done slowly enough to also discover vehicles, WAiNK It spots and meditation spots on the same trip.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob an illegal operation belonging to each gang — one operation per gang, all 9 gangs, so a single gang's turf is not enough. Illegal operations are the gangs' off-the-books businesses; hit one for each gang and the trophy pops. Learn which gangs hold which turf first, then work the list gang by gang. It pairs with the other crime trophies, since the same planning — approach, grab, escape — applies to every robbery on the list.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach — walk to a bar on Ocean Beach, order a cocktail, and take in the view. It is the calmest trophy on the list and deliberately so: a quiet moment after the noise. Any beachfront bar works; sit, drink, and let the trophy pop. Save it for the cleanup stage as a breather between the money grinds.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style — drive a car straight through the showroom glass and out the other side, the way the old games taught you. Pick a fast car, line up on the showroom, and go through it without stopping. It is a one-move trophy: the setup is the whole job, so save first, then commit to the run.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Follow through at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley — play a full game of bowling there, follow-through and all. It is one of the 9 activity types, so it also feeds Master of None: visit the alley during the stage-2 activity sweep, bowl a game, and both trophies move. No score target — finishing the game is enough.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: Reach a partnership moment with mass appeal — flagged missable because it hinges on a specific partnership beat during the story, not a grind you can return to. It happens when a partnership moment plays out in front of a crowd; play the story beats that involve your partner and let the moment come. Save before any big partnership scene so a missed beat costs nothing.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Make choices — PlayStation tracks them toward a count of 500, so this is a long-horizon trophy, flagged missable because choices lock in as the story moves on. The practical approach is to play naturally and make the choices the story offers, checking the tracked count as you go; there is no single moment to farm, only the accumulated decisions of the whole playthrough. Do not rush the story if the count is lagging — the choices are the content.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Succeed on the second try — flagged missable because it is a single second-chance moment: fail something once, then succeed at the very next attempt. The honest way to get it is to let it happen: when a mission or activity fails, retry it immediately and finish it. Do not engineer failures across the game; the moment comes on its own, and the trophy pops when the retry lands.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: Witness something strange — flagged missable because it is a one-off weird event, not a checklist item you can hunt on demand. Strange things happen in Leonida when you go looking: remote places, odd hours, and the corners of the map where the game hides its jokes. Roam the far edges of the state during the cleanup stage and let the event find you; when something unexplainable happens, the trophy pops.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl them over with a melee drive-by — knock someone down with a melee attack from a moving vehicle. The trick is speed plus timing: drive past on a bike or in a slow car, swing as you pass, and keep moving. It is easier in traffic, where pedestrians are close to the road, than on open highway. A few passes usually lands it.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts — the money total is tracked, so it grows with every laundered batch. Marked Bills come from the crime side of the game, so this trophy is the payoff for the stage-4 heists: rob, launder, repeat. It is a late-game number by design — do not chase it early, let the heist income flow through your contacts and the total will cross $250,000 during cleanup.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops — every shop in Leonida counts toward the one total, so spread the spending: clothes, weapons, car mods, food, whatever the game sells. The fastest route is the expensive end of the catalogue: a few big purchases move the total more than a hundred small ones. It pairs with the money trophies — earn through heists, spend through shops, and the two totals rise together.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all 8 garage properties — every garage the game sells, so the count only completes when the last one is bought. Garages are bought with the money the heists earn, which is why this sits in stage 3 of the roadmap but is usually finished in cleanup: buy them as the cash allows, and keep the most expensive one for last so the spending feeds Treat Yo Self too.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — ten different vehicles, registered through the app. The app is the in-world way to claim a vehicle as yours: drive something worth keeping, open Scooter Bros, and register it. It pairs with Whip It Good, since every vehicle you discover is a candidate to register; register the ten you like best and the trophy pops.
